items.title: Dawki Fish Market
items.description: Riverside market at Dawki where fish caught in the Umngot and traded from Bangladesh arrive early morning. The Umngot is a major source of mahseer and carp; watching the morning fish auction and local trade at a border-river town is an authentic local experience. The market is also the informal hub of Dawki's cross-border commerce. Best visited between 06:30 and 09:00. Free to browse.
items.reasoning: Start the morning with an authentic local experience at the Dawki Fish Market by the river.

items.title: Umngot River Boating
items.description: Boating on the Umngot River, celebrated as one of the clearest rivers in India. In the Oct–Apr dry season the water is so transparent that boats appear to float in mid-air above the riverbed — a widely photographed optical illusion. Coracle-style wooden boats are hired from local boatmen at the riverside ghat; no fixed rate, negotiate on the spot. The river forms the India-Bangladesh border; boats do not cross into Bangladesh. Most dramatic on sunny mornings when reflections are sharp. Avoid Jul–Sep monsoon when river is high and muddy.
items.reasoning: Experience the famous transparent boat ride on the Umngot River during the best morning lighting.

items.title: Dawki Suspension Bridge
items.description: Long suspension bridge crossing the Umngot River at Dawki, used by cross-border trade trucks. Built in the colonial era; the current structure is maintained by the Indian government. Walking across provides a good vantage point for photographing the turquoise river below. The bridge also forms the visual backdrop for most Umngot boat photographs. Free to walk across. Located directly adjacent to the main boat-hire ghat.
items.reasoning: Walk across the adjacent Dawki Suspension Bridge for panoramic views and photos of the turquoise river.

items.title: Dawki Riverside Picnic Food
items.description: Dawki has basic roadside stalls near the Umngot River serving Khasi snacks, boiled eggs, chai, and simple rice meals. The best strategy is to buy from Shillong or Cherrapunji before arrival and picnic by the crystal-clear green river while watching boats cross to Bangladesh.
items.reasoning: Enjoy a relaxing riverside picnic lunch near the bridge with local Khasi snacks and views.

items.title: Tamabil Border Crossing Viewpoint
items.description: Viewpoint at the Tamabil (Bangladesh)–Dawki (India) integrated check post, one of the busiest land border crossings between India and Bangladesh. Cross-border trade in fish, limestone, and goods is conducted here. Foreign nationals with valid Bangladesh entry visas may cross; Indian nationals require ICP approval. Watching the lorries and commerce at an active Himalayan foothills border crossing is a unique local experience. Photographing the border check post directly is restricted.
items.reasoning: Conclude the afternoon sightseeing with a visit to the Tamabil Border Crossing Viewpoint nearby.
